title: Partial Functions with Panicking Paths
pattern: A function signature claiming to return a pure type `T` but containing implicit execution paths that panic or crash when presented with valid input boundary states.
why_bad: Partial functions lie in their signatures. They claim they can successfully return a `T` for any array, forcing callers to manually verify pre-conditions, which is highly error-prone and leads to unexpected runtime crashes.
detection: Functions returning non-Option/non-Result types containing `panic!`, `unwrap()`, or unsafe indexing (`[0]`) on inputs whose boundaries are not checked.
source: *Type-Driven Development with Idris* by Edwin Brady (Chapter 2, p. 59); *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 42).
